::: {.site-shell .academic-shell}

```{=html}
<header class="page-hero academic-hero">
  <p class="page-eyebrow">Academic</p>
  <h2 class="one-page-title">Economic Methodologist and Innovation Economist</h2>
</header>

<section class="main-card academic-about-card">
  <p>Economics and computational modelling are at the core of my research. I study how models and simulations are designed, evaluated, and used to explain complex economic and social phenomena and inform decision-making. My work combines economic methodology and agent-based modelling, with applications to innovation dynamics, knowledge diffusion, model selection, causal interpretation, and model credibility.</p>
  <p>I also investigate institutional and algorithmic decision-making, participatory methods, and methodological issues in survey and experimental research. Across these areas, I focus on how assumptions, research design, and modelling choices affect the reliability, interpretation, and practical use of results.</p>
  <p class="academic-about-card__contact"><a class="action-link" href="mailto:massimo.rusconi@uninsubria.it">massimo.rusconi@uninsubria.it</a></p>
</section>
```

## Research Interests

```{=html}
<div class="theme-grid" aria-label="Research interests">
  <article class="soft-card theme-card">
    <h3>Models and evaluation</h3>
    <p>Model credibility, model selection, analogy, causal interpretation and the epistemology of simulation.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="soft-card theme-card">
    <h3>Simulation and innovation</h3>
    <p>Agent-based modelling, social simulation, innovation dynamics, knowledge production and system learning. I use NetLogo to develop and explore agent-based simulation models.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="soft-card theme-card">
    <h3>Institutions and methods</h3>
    <p>Algorithmic decision-making, participatory methods, and methodological problems in survey and experimental research.</p>
  </article>
</div>
```

## Publications

### Published and Accepted Peer-Reviewed Journal Articles {.unlisted}

```{=html}
<div class="publication-grid" aria-label="Published and accepted peer-reviewed journal articles">
  <article class="record-card publication-card">
    <div class="publication-card__header">
      <span class="status-badge">Journal article</span>
      <span class="publication-card__year">2026</span>
    </div>
    <h4>Model trustworthiness and modeler responsibility in economic agent-based modeling practices: A meta-analytical approach</h4>
    <p class="publication-card__authors">Rusconi, M., Secchi, D., &amp; Seri, R.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__meta"><em>Journal of Economic Methodology</em>, 1-21. Published article.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__description">Examines credibility and trustworthiness in economic agent-based modelling, emphasising the modeller's responsibility for aligning purposes, targets and modelling strategies. It proposes a meta-analytical framework for reducing model mistargeting and misuse through greater transparency and consistency.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__actions"><a class="action-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1080/1350178X.2026.2617538">DOI</a></p>
  </article>

  <article class="record-card publication-card">
    <div class="publication-card__header">
      <span class="status-badge">Journal article</span>
      <span class="publication-card__year">2026</span>
    </div>
    <h4>Investigating the analytical robustness of the social and behavioural sciences</h4>
    <p class="publication-card__authors">Aczel, B., Szaszi, B., K&oacute;sa, L. et al.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__meta"><em>Nature</em>. Published article.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__actions"><a class="action-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09844-9">DOI</a></p>
  </article>

  <article class="record-card publication-card">
    <div class="publication-card__header">
      <span class="status-badge">Journal article</span>
      <span class="publication-card__year">2025</span>
    </div>
    <h4>The analogical roots of agent-based modeling in economics and social sciences: The case of innovation dynamics</h4>
    <p class="publication-card__authors">Rusconi, M., Secchi, D., &amp; Seri, R.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__meta"><em>Journal of Economic Methodology</em>, 1-24. Published article.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__description">Develops an analogical framework for evaluating the conceptual adequacy of economic agent-based models across their conceptual, algorithmic and computational layers. The framework is applied to the SKIN and K+S families of innovation models.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__actions"><a class="action-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1080/1350178X.2025.2547639">DOI</a></p>
  </article>

  <article class="record-card publication-card">
    <div class="publication-card__header">
      <span class="status-badge">Journal article</span>
      <span class="publication-card__year">2025</span>
    </div>
    <h4>Investigating conspiracy beliefs: methodological biases and experimental challenges</h4>
    <p class="publication-card__authors">Gagliardi, L., &amp; Rusconi, M.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__meta"><em>Journal of Economic Methodology</em>, 1-21. Published article.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__description">Reviews methodological biases in research on conspiracy beliefs, focusing on social-desirability effects, survey spillovers and the limitations of explicit self-reported measures. It also examines the conceptual and practical difficulties involved in developing survey-free experimental approaches.</p>
    <p class="publication-card__actions"><a class="action-link" href="https://doi.org/10.1080/1350178X.2025.2539253">DOI</a></p>
  </article>
</div>
```
